findings.title: Caller-supplied AbortSignal is silently discarded (cancellation regression)
findings.evidence: The spread places `...options` first and then hard-sets `signal: controller.signal`, so any `signal` the caller passed is dropped.
findings.evidence_quote: const response = await fetch(url, { ...options, signal: controller.signal });
findings.recommendation: Preserve and combine the caller signal, e.g. `const signal = options.signal ? AbortSignal.any([options.signal, controller.signal]) : controller.signal;` and pass that; drop `options.signal` from the spread or overwrite it explicitly. Add a test that aborting a caller-provided controller cancels the request.

findings.title: timeoutMs is unvalidated; 0, null or Infinity abort effectively immediately
findings.evidence: `timeoutMs` goes straight into `setTimeout`; the default only applies for `undefined`, so `timeoutMs: null` becomes 0 and `timeoutMs: Infinity` is clamped by the runtime to 1ms in Node.
findings.recommendation: Validate the value (e.g. require a finite number > 0, or treat non-finite/<=0 as 'no timeout' by skipping setTimeout) and throw a clear TypeError for invalid values.

findings.title: Timeout is indistinguishable from other aborts; no diagnostic error
findings.evidence: The abort reason is not recorded; the caller just receives the runtime's generic AbortError with no indication it was the 8s timeout.
findings.recommendation: Track whether the timer fired (a boolean flag or `controller.abort(new Error('timeout after ' + timeoutMs + 'ms'))`) and rethrow a descriptive timeout error from the catch path so callers can distinguish timeout from network failure.

findings.title: No tests were run for new timing/abort behaviour
findings.evidence: The change adds a new asynchronous timeout branch and a `finally` cleanup, and the report states no test commands were run, so neither the abort path nor the timer cleanup is exercised.
findings.recommendation: Add tests using a slow/never-resolving fetch stub and fake timers: assert the promise rejects on timeout, that the timer is cleared on success (no leaked handle), and that a caller-supplied signal still cancels.
